newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LME copper rise eases pressure on S.Korean buyers.
newsitem.headline: LME copper rise eases pressure on S.Korean buyers.

text.p: South Korean metal traders breathed a sigh of relief at sharp gains in London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices, but warned on Monday that buyers could still face big losses if prices fall back.

The LME rally has cut the size of loss-making positions being rolled forward by South Korean traders and their clients since the market tumbled after the annoucement by Japan's Sumitomo Corp in June of huge trading losses incurred in unauthorised copper trading.
"Our clients seem to be relieved by the recent price rise," a trader with Tong Yang Futures said, adding that most South Korean copper companies are traditionally long-position takers.
"Some LME users carried their loss bearing postions forward from September when the copper market was in contango," said another trader, who asked not to be named.
"One of them carried a loss-bearing position, done in a single day, of over 1,000 lots (25,000 tonnes) to December," he added.
By using so-called Non-Market Price Transactions (NMPT), metal clients can carry forward their loss positions based on their existing contract prices, traders said.
However, these clients have to pay costs to their counterparties for the financing period and for premiums or discounts based on the prevailing market sitation.

Other South Korean clients are in the happier position of having granted copper put options last September with strike prices between $1,700 and $1,900 a tonne for expiry in December, the Tong Yang trader said.
"These clients are enjoying profits from their options positions," he said.
"One client granted puts of over 1,000 to 2,000 tonnes a day when prices remained at around $1,900," a trader with LG Futures Co Ltd said.

Three month LME copper was approaching $2,200 a tonne in early trade on Monday. On Friday the contract rose $117 a tonne to $2,148 after LME copper stocks fell to a new 6-1/4 year low of 101,175 tonnes.
The cash to three-month backwardation widened to $105/$115 a tonne from $80/$85 from a day earlier.

South Korean traders said the NMPT system could cause a snowballing of copper loss among local companies who do not have tight control over their futures operations if the current upward trend in LME copper prices again reverses.
"What we normally do is to clear out profit-bearing positions and get the profit in first. Then we carry forward loss-bearing positions as long as possible," one trader said.

The proceeds from settling profit-making positions are invested in domestic money markets to earn more than 11 percent interest, while financing loss-bearing positions incur London Interbank Offered Rates of around 5.5 percent, traders said.
